risk_factors.heading: Cyclical industry and decline in production levels of major customers
risk_factors.quote: Our sales are driven by the number of vehicles produced by our automotive manufacturer customers and our content per vehicle. The automotive industry is cyclical and sensitive to general economic conditions

risk_factors.heading: Cyclical industry and decline in production levels of major customers
risk_factors.quote: As these traditional automakers are among our largest customers, our business and financial results may be adversely affected by decreases in their businesses or market share.

risk_factors.heading: Increases in costs and availability of raw materials, energy, components and labor
risk_factors.quote: Raw material, energy, commodity, product component and labor costs can be volatile. Although we have developed and implemented strategies to mitigate the impact of any such cost increases

risk_factors.heading: Failure to execute strategic objectives
risk_factors.quote: risk factors include our failure to identify suitable opportunities for organic investment and/or acquisitions, our inability to successfully develop such opportunities or complete such acquisitions or our inability to successfully utilize or integrate the investments in our operations.

risk_factors.heading: Lack of commercial success or directed sourcing for key vehicle models
risk_factors.quote: It is possible that a particular vehicle model is not successful with consumers or that our customers elect to manufacture our products internally, purchase our products from other suppliers

risk_factors.heading: Inability to offset customer-imposed price reductions
risk_factors.quote: Downward pricing pressure by automotive manufacturers is a characteristic of the automotive industry. Our customer contracts generally provide for annual price reductions over the production life of the vehicle

risk_factors.heading: International trade policies, tariffs, sanctions and export controls
risk_factors.quote: many of the tariffs announced, implemented or threatened by the current U.S. administration apply to (a) the countries in which we do business or from which we purchase, either directly or indirectly, materials or components, including China, Mexico and Canada
